result.summary: This is not a repair job. The landlord reports rent arrears and a dispute over a deposit from a previous tenancy, and asks for the locks to be changed so the tenant can't get in until he pays. That would be a likely unlawful eviction. I did not arrange a locksmith. I escalated the case at high priority to a person in the lettings team, emailed the landlord to say the case has been passed on and not to change the locks, and recorded the reported dispute on the property.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 412: the landlord wants the locks changed 'so he cannot get in until he pays'. Locking out a tenant who still lives there without a court order is likely unlawful eviction under the Protection from Eviction Act 1977. Rent arrears and deposit disputes are matters for a person, not maintenance tools. The intake note (event 413) says no defect was reported. classify_reply returned 'review' (needs a human response 0.94, dissatisfied 0.57).
